source_text: Nihil studii exspectari ab humana voluntate debere, contra illud evangelicum quo ait Dominus: Petite, et accipietis; quaerite, et invenietis; pulsate, et aperietur vobis: omnis enim qui petit, accipit; et qui quaerit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur
pass_a_gloss: Nothing studii exspectari from humana by-will to-owe, against that evangelicum whither he-says Lord: Petite, and accipietis; quaerite, and invenietis; pulsate, and aperietur to-you: all for who petit, receives; and who quaerit, invenit; and pulsanti aperietur.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: [He says] that no effort should be expected from the human will, contrary to the Gospel, where the Lord says: “Ask, and you will receive; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives; whoever seeks finds; and to the one who knocks it will be opened” (Matthew 7:7–8).

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
